title: ATONEMENT
mv: For He made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us, that we might become the righteousness of God in Him.
mvp: “For He made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us, that we might become the righteousness of God in Him.” 2 Corinthians 5:21 (NKJV)
assignment: Write five (5) practical ways the sacrifice of Jesus has transformed or is transforming your life (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: Atonement is the process or act of making amends for a wrong, harm or injury. It is an avenue for up timing reconciliation between man and God through the price, sacrifice and suffering of Jesus Christ on the cross. With this, the condemned sinner is justified by grace and recognised as a saint. This lesson enlightens the church on the weight of Christ’s sacrifice and the accrued benefits.
Atonement is what we got when Jesus took the place of man on the cross and endured an excruciating death that is due to man (Romans 5:8; 1 John 4:10).
The core components of this atonement include:

i: Sacrifice: The act of giving a life as an offering to pay for sins (Ephesians 5:2).
Substitution: Christ took the place of man to bear the punishment for sin (2 Corinthians 5:21; Galatians 3:13).
Redemption: The act of paying a price to free someone from an obligation or sin (Ephesians 1:7; Hebrews 9:12).
Propitiation: An action intended to appease a deity, or to change their attitude in a more positive direction. Propitiation connotes the process of appeasing God’s wrath (Romans 3:25; 1John 2:2).

Satisfaction: The idea that a debt must be paid, and atonement involves satisfying this debt through a sufficient offering (Romans 6:23; Hebrews 9:26). The Bible declares that Christ's suffering, beginning from the Garden of Gethsemane to the point he died on the cross, is sufficient and no other sacrifice is required (Hebrews 10:10-14).
Reconciliation: The restoration of a relationship, which is a goal or result of atonement (Romans 5:10; 2 Corinthians 5:18-19).

b.x: To partake of the provision of atonement, a sinner must confess his sins with his mouth (1John 1:9) and decide to forsake his old sinful lifestyle (Proverbs 28:13; Ephesians 4:22-24).
There are several benefits derived from atonement; a few will suffice here:

i: Atonement offers divine forgiveness, and brings indescribable peace to the human recipient (Colossians 1:20).
Atonement turned away the wrath of God from believers (Psalm 85:2-3, John 3:36).
It facilitates reconciliation through the sacrifice of Jesus. Turning human condemnation to divine justification (Romans 3:24).
Atonement makes assurance of salvation possible with the attendant confidence (Romans 8:1).
It makes impartation of righteousness a possibility and reality, and we become empowered to live above sin (2 Corinthians 5:21).

b.x: Believers must know that a price was paid for their salvation, and hence this sacrifice must not be taken for granted (Hebrews 6:4-6).
